First, let $f(x)=\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x$ and $g(x)=-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x & =-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x \\ 3{x}^{2}+5x & =-2{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+5x \\ 2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/d19b70836b7b377c498fa505868563115706b588b0a2216d09c6ec738f746bbd.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=f(x)=\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=g(x)=-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x]-[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(-{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{2})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2\pi [(-\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{2}^{4}}{2})-0] \\  & =2\pi (-\frac{32}{5}+8) \\  & =2\pi \cdot \frac{8}{5} \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$
